query: I'm designing a new 'Segmented control' for our Figma library because our Tabs don't fit filter toggles. Can you spec it for me?
expected_behavior: Checks first whether an existing component or variant (Tabs, Toggle button group, Filter chips) can do the job and frames this as a contribution request with use cases from multiple teams
Defines anatomy, variants and properties whose names match the coded component API
Designs every relevant state: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, selected, read-only, plus combinations like selected + focus
Maps parts to component tokens that alias semantic tokens and specifies density, responsive behavior, and 24 px minimum targets

Includes accessibility (keyboard model, accessible names, 3:1 focus and boundaries, selection not shown by color alone) and uses the component documentation template from reference/component-docs-and-governance.md

query: We're setting up color tokens for our design system and want dark mode later. How should we name and structure them in Figma variables?
expected_behavior: Recommends three tiers - primitive, semantic, component - with purpose-based names such as color.action.primary.bg.hover rather than appearance-based names
Sets up Figma variable collections with hidden primitives and semantic modes for Light, Dark, and High contrast, scoped appropriately
Requires contrast validation for every semantic pair in every theme (4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI components and focus)
Gives a small token JSON or table example and lists common naming mistakes

query: Here's my design for the user management page for admins - can you check it against our design system before I hand off to engineering?
expected_behavior: Runs the design QA checklist from reference/component-docs-and-governance.md
Checks the table, filters, and bulk actions against reference/enterprise-patterns.md (sticky header, filter chips, count in bulk action labels, partial-failure handling)
Flags detached instances, raw values, and missing states such as first-use empty, no results, loading, error, and no-permission
Verifies role-based views, the destructive confirmation pattern for deactivating users, and accessibility annotations
Returns findings in the output template with deviations annotated and gaps logged as contributions
